thread:
incident-bot: ALERT ─ KV cache eviction & paging spike detected on runtime-prod-*-pool at 2024-04-12T03:12Z. Evictions/s ↑ 14x, page_in/s ↑ 9x, p95 latency ↑ 85ms -> 420ms. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

sam: I'm on it. Seeing correlated increase with recent int8 kernel selector rollout (autoselect -> awq/gptq path) around 03:05Z.

maya: Confirmed. Continuous-batching throughput also jumped, which seems to populate more KV entries per request. Might be an interaction: quant path changed per-token kv size.

deepak: Paging is mainly on nvme-2 for the pool. I can throttle eviction proactively. Putting a banner on affected customers.

leila: @sam @maya tagging @eng-runtime-ic. Any quick rollback options for the kernel selector?

eng-runtime-ic: We can set per-cluster kernel fallback env var to force the previous fp16-compatible kernels. Quick command: 
```
POST /internal/features/runtime/kernel_selector
{"cluster":"runtime-prod-1","strategy":"prefer_fp16_for_int8"}
```
But needs approvals + rolling restart for workers to pick it up.

jordan: Can we avoid restarts by patching the routing rule to route new requests to model-variants that use the older kernel? That would be lower blast.

maria: Customer impact: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, wavepay) reported 5xx spikes and slow streaming for long chat sessions. CS alerted.

sam: Short term mitigation I propose: 1) reduce continuous-batcher.max_window_ms to 20ms 2) set continuous-batcher.max_batch_tokens=512 3) temporarily limit cache.max_entries per-session to 1k. These are dynamic flags and don't require restart. Implementing now.

ops-bot: ACTION: applied flag continuous-batcher.max_window_ms=20 on runtime-prod-*-pool at 03:22Z.

sam: Throttle applied. Watching metrics. Evictions/s down ~40% in the last 3m. Paging still high but plateauing.

maya: Good. Parallel: eng-runtime-ic, please stage kernel_selector fallback in canary. We want to validate KV footprint difference between awq/gptq int8 path and fp16-preferring path.

eng-runtime-ic: Canary running on 3 nodes. Initial histograms show avg per-request kv_size_bytes dropped ~28% when forcing fp16 kernels. That matches a theory: the awq int8 backend packs KV differently (larger key rows) causing >2x per-token footprint at certain sequence lengths.

deepak: We're seeing IO pressure reduce on nvme-2 as canary nodes start serving traffic. Nice.

leila: Customer comms: @maria please send an update that we're mitigating and throttling batching to reduce memory/IO pressure, and that a kernel-fallback is being staged. ETA for broader rollout ~30–45m after verification.

maria: Drafting now. Will ping legal for wording on root cause if asked.

sam: Next step: if canary verifies, we do a staged kernel_selector override across other worker pools with controlled ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Ops runbook step: pause autoscaler during rollout to avoid weird capacity churn.

jordan: Note — rolling kernel change will not change model params, only runtime kernel selection. Watches: kv_cache_size_bytes, evictions/s, p95 latency, 5xx rate.

ops-bot: METRIC SNAPSHOT (03:40Z): runtime-prod: page_in/s 920 -> 460 (post-batching throttle), evictions/s 1120 -> 520, p95 latency 420ms -> 310ms.

eng-runtime-ic: Canary looks stable at 03:46Z. Per-request KV median ~2.6KB -> 1.9KB. I'm pushing kernel_selector to runtime-prod-1 at 03:48Z (10% traffic).

sam: Rolling now. Remember to set `autoscaler.paused=true` on pools while ramping.

ops-bot: ACTION: autoscaler.paused=true on runtime-prod-1 at 03:49Z.

maya: After 10% ramp: evictions/s down another 15%, p95 down to ~260ms. No increase in 5xx observed on canary.

leila: Good. Ramp to 50% now. Ops monitor please.

ops-bot: ACTION: kernel_selector update applied to 50% traffic at 03:57Z.

sam: At 50%: page_in/s ~220, evictions/s ~180, p95 ~200ms. Looks like kernel selection change is effective.

maria: Notifying impacted customers: "We've applied a mitigation that reduces memory pressure on the runtime; you may see improved latency within minutes. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a post-incident summary." :white_check_mark:

deepak: Rolling to 100% at 04:05Z. Also re-enabling autoscaler after rollout.

ops-bot: ACTION: kernel_selector fully applied to runtime-prod-*. autoscaler.paused=false at 04:07Z.

sam: Final metrics at 04:10Z: page_in/s back to baseline range, evictions/s low, p95 at 120–160ms. 5xx rates returned to normal.

maria: CS update sent to impacted customers at 04:12Z.

eng-runtime-ic: Root cause notes for postmortem: awq/gptq int8 kernel autoselect introduced a packing/layout change for KV storage resulting in larger per-token KV footprints at medium-long sequence lengths. This interacts badly with continuous-batching because more tokens are batched/preserved in KV cache leading to eviction storms and NVMe paging.

jordan: Follow-ups assigned: 1) make kernel_selector integration tests check kv footprint across quant paths (owner: eng-runtime) 2) add alerting on kv_size_bytes per-request moving median (owner: eng-sre) 3) add safeguard to continuous-batcher that will fall back to single-request mode if per-request kv growth beyond threshold (owner: eng-ml).

leila: Also add customer-facing RCA template so we can push faster comms.

sam: Handoff to postmortem. Oncall summary: mitigation applied (batching throttle + kernel_selector fallback), metrics recovered, customers notified. No data loss.

incident-bot: INCIDENT -> status: mitigated. Handoff to postmortem channel.

maria: I'll coordinate the postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks everyone. :pray:

sam: Closing thread, will attach dashboards + commands used to the postmortem doc.

-- end of thread --
